Key Terms

restricted stock unitsfinancial
Restricted stock units are a type of company reward where employees are promised shares of stock, but they only fully own these shares after meeting certain conditions, like staying with the company for a set time. They matter because they can become valuable assets and are often used to motivate employees to help the company succeed.
non-qualified stock optionfinancial
A non-qualified stock option (NSO) is a contract that lets an employee or service provider buy company shares at a fixed price for a set period, like a voucher to purchase stock later at today’s price. It matters to investors because exercising NSOs creates ordinary income for the holder and can increase share count, affecting a company’s earnings and ownership mix; think of it as a future sale that can dilute existing shareholders and has immediate tax consequences for the recipient.

NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) is a rule that requires a company to get approval from its shareholders before selling a large amount of its shares, usually over 20%. AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Vital Farms (Nasdaq: VITL) announced today the pilot launch of Vital Farms Free-Range eggs, which are expected to arrive in select Target retail stores across the South and Southeast beginning this week.

This limited test is designed to explore how Vital Farms can reach more households with a high-quality product at a more accessible suggested retail price point of less than $5 per carton, while maintaining its commitment to transparency and animal welfare.

Introducing A New Vital Farms Standard

“Free-range” is one of the most familiar terms in the egg aisle, but the standard itself doesn’t consistently tell consumers what they are actually buying. Compared with many other free-range products, the new Vital Farms Free-Range standard sets a higher bar for animal welfare in several meaningful areas: time outside, better land with living vegetation and shade, and barns designed to make it easier for hens to head outdoors. And like every carton of Vital Farms eggs, each carton can be traced back to the farm where the eggs were laid through the company’s “See The Farm” program.

This new Vital Farms standard for free-range reflects Vital Farms’ commitments to animal care, product quality, and transparency. Vital Farms loves hearing from consumers with questions. Visit vitalfarms.com/contact for details on how to call, text, direct message or write, or visit Vital Farms’ Frequently Asked Questions page to learn more.

Living Within Vital Farms’ Values and Testing Something New

“With Vital Farms Free-Range, we’re testing how we can bring more households a high-quality egg at a more accessible price point, while staying true to who we are and keeping hens’ quality of life front and center,” said Heather Mace, Vital Farms Vice President, Brand. “Our goal is to learn all we can, understand consumer appetite and grow the right way. Reaching more households gives us the opportunity to create more positive impact for our stakeholders while continuing to raise the standards in the egg aisle.”

Vital Farms Free-Range eggs are expected to be available beginning this week at select Target retail stores across the South and Southeast. For more information on where to find Vital Farms eggs, please visit: https://vitalfarms.com/where-to-buy/

ABOUT VITAL FARMS:

Vital Farms (Nasdaq: VITL) is a Certified B Corporation that offers a range of ethically produced foods nationwide. Started on a single farm in Austin, Texas, in 2007, Vital Farms is now a national consumer brand that works with 600 small farms and is the leading U.S. brand of pasture-raised eggs by retail dollar sales. Vital Farms’ ethics are exemplified by its focus on the humane treatment of farm animals and sustainable farming practices. In addition, as a Delaware public benefit corporation, Vital Farms prioritizes the long-term benefits of each of its stakeholders, including farmers and suppliers, customers and consumers, communities and the environment, and crew members and stockholders. Vital Farms’ products, including shell eggs, hard-boiled eggs, and liquid whole eggs, are sold in more than 24,000 stores nationwide. Vital Farms pasture-raised eggs can also be found on menus at hundreds of foodservice operators across the country. For more information, visit https://vitalfarms.com.

TOKYO, JP / ACCESS Newswire / October 24, 2026 / Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. (Nasdaq:LAWR) ("Robot Consulting" or the "Company"), a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions and legal technology, announced it has received a delisting determination from the Listing Qualifications Department (the "Staff") of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying the Company of the Staff's determination to delist the Company's American Depository Shares ("ADSs") pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rules 5101 and IM-5101-4.

The Staff's determination is based on concerns regarding historical trading activity in the Company's securities and Nasdaq's belief that certain factors may have made the Company's securities susceptible to manipulation by third parties.

Nasdaq Listing Rule IM-5101-4 allows Nasdaq "to exercise discretion to delist a company from Nasdaq based on the potential for one or more third parties to engage in misconduct impacting a company's securities where the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission] has implemented a temporary trading suspension." Nasdaq has articulated its belief that the ability for third parties to manipulate a security's price indicates that the security does not have sufficient liquidity to promote fair and orderly markets and, therefore, delisting is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.

The Company has appealed the Staff's determination to a Hearings Panel (the "Panel") on October 23, 2026. As a result of the appeal, the suspension of the Company's securities and the filing of the Form 25-NSE by Nasdaq with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") will be stayed pending the Panel's review and decision, although the existing trading halt will remain in effect unless and until it has been lifted by Nasdaq.

To date, Nasdaq has not claimed or communicated a view that there has been any wrongdoing by the Company, whether in regard to Nasdaq's investigation of the recent trading activity of the Company's securities or otherwise. The delisting determination does not have any immediate effect on the Company's ongoing business operations or financial condition, and the Company will continue to conduct its business in the ordinary course.

About Robot Consulting Co., Ltd.

Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. is a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions with an intention to expand into legal technology. The Company's major product, "Labor Robot," is a cloud-based human resource management system that helps users track employee attendance, manage sales orders, and journalize accounting items. Robot Consulting also assists users with grant and subsidy applications and provides consulting and support services for digital transformation to small and medium-sized businesses. Robot Consulting also aims to create more software and services related to digital transformation and legal technology. The Company has launched "Robot Lawyer," a platform that provides preliminary legal consultation resources to individuals and small businesses, particularly with respect to defamatory online posts or other reputational harm. For more information, visit www.robotconsulting.net.

BETHESDA, Md., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Elme Communities (“Elme” or the “Company”) today announced that the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) has exercised its discretionary authority in accordance with Section 802.01D of the NYSE Listed Company Manual to commence proceedings to delist Elme’s common shares of beneficial interest (the “Common Shares”) from the NYSE due to “abnormally low selling price” levels. The NYSE also immediately suspended trading of the Common Shares. Given the Company’s previously adopted Plan of Sale and Liquidation (as defined below), Elme does not intend to appeal the NYSE’s determination, and, therefore, it is expected that the Common Shares will be delisted. 

The Company anticipates the Common Shares will commence trading over-the-counter (“OTC”) on Monday, October 26, 2026 under the symbol “ELMES”. There can be no assurance regarding the development or maintenance of an active OTC trading market or the liquidity of any such market. Investors are cautioned that trading securities OTC is more limited and subject to different restrictions than trading securities listed on a national securities exchange and are advised to consult their own brokers or advisors.

Anticipated Timing of Establishment of a Liquidating Trust and Company Dissolution

As previously disclosed, in accordance with the Plan of Sale and Liquidation approved by the Board of Trustees (the “Board”) on July 30, 2025 and by the shareholders of the Company on October 30, 2025 (the “Plan of Sale and Liquidation”), it is the Company’s continued intention to terminate its existence by voluntary dissolution effective November 6, 2026 (the “Effective Time”), which will occur following the NYSE’s delisting of our Common Shares. In addition, as previously disclosed, the Company expects that its share transfer books will close at the close of business (Eastern Time) on November 5, 2026.

Prior to the Effective Time, the Company intends to transfer all of its remaining assets and liabilities to a Maryland liquidating trust (the “Liquidating Trust”). The purpose of the Liquidating Trust will be to liquidate the remaining assets (which are expected to consist primarily of the net cash proceeds from property sales) of the Liquidating Trust and distribute the amounts remaining in the Liquidating Trust, if any, after satisfaction of all remaining liabilities (including any additional liabilities, costs and expenses that may arise during the wind-down process) to the holders of the beneficial interests of the Liquidating Trust (the “Beneficial Interests”) upon completion of the wind-down process and in connection with termination of the Liquidating Trust. All of the Beneficial Interests will be held by the shareholders of the Company, with each shareholder of the Company being deemed automatically to have received and hold a percentage of Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust corresponding to such shareholder’s percentage ownership in the Company as of the close of business on the last day of trading of the Common Shares. Shareholders of the Company will not be required to take any action to receive Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust. The actual amount and timing of payment of any additional liquidating distribution(s) from the Liquidating Trust will be determined by the trustee of the Liquidating Trust in their sole discretion. As previously disclosed, the Company expects FTI Consulting, Inc. to be retained to provide services in connection with completing the wind-down process, including the services of a liquidating trustee to serve as trustee of the Liquidating Trust.

Following the transfer of the Company’s assets and liabilities to the Liquidating Trust, subject to certain exceptions related to transfer by will, intestate succession or operation of law, Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust will not be transferable, nor will holders of Beneficial Interests have authority or power to sell or in any other manner dispose of their Beneficial Interests. data.title: Travere Presents New Biomarker Data at ASN Kidney Week Suggesting FILSPARI® (sparsentan) May Modify Underlying Disease Pathophysiology in IgA Nephropathy | TVTX Stock News
data.description:
The biomarker analysis adds biological findings to previously reported urine-protein and kidney-function results.

See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers.Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google
Add on Google

FILSPARI achieved greater reductions in biomarkers linked to kidney inflammation and injury than maximum labeled dose irbesartan

Findings provide further evidence of the biological effects of dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism and support FILSPARI as foundational treatment in IgAN 

SAN DIEGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Travere Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TVTX) today presented new biomarker data from the Phase 3 PROTECT Study providing evidence that FILSPARI® (sparsentan) may modify the underlying disease pathophysiology in people with IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Data were shared today in an oral presentation at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, CO.

“These biomarker data provide new insight into how FILSPARI’s dual mechanism of action may modify the underlying biology of IgA nephropathy,” said Jula Inrig, M.D., chief medical officer of Travere Therapeutics. “When considered alongside the PROTECT results which demonstrated superior proteinuria reduction and a slower rate of kidney function decline compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan, as well as published real-world evidence showing consistent outcomes in clinical practice, the totality of evidence supports the use of FILSPARI as a non-immunosuppressive, kidney-targeted, foundational first-line treatment for IgA nephropathy.”

The Phase 3 PROTECT Study was a global, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of FILSPARI, compared to irbesartan in 404 adult patients with IgAN. Of the overall study population, 295 patients participated in the biomarker analysis. Across measured time points through Week 110, FILSPARI led to rapid and sustained reductions in all four urinary biomarkers evaluated.

“These findings extend the exploratory signal observed in SPARTAN and show in a larger, randomized study that dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism may modulate several biological pathways associated with IgAN pathophysiology,” said Chee Kay Cheung, M.B.Ch.B., Ph.D., consultant nephrologist at University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust.

At Week 110, least-squares mean percent changes from baseline, normalized to urine creatinine, were greater with FILSPARI than with irbesartan (reported p values are nominal):

  • sCD163, a marker of macrophage activation, decreased 60.1% with FILSPARI versus 26.0% with irbesartan, representing a 46.1% difference between treatment arms (p<0.001).
  • BAFF, a marker of B-cell activation and survival, decreased 64.4% with FILSPARI versus 45.2% with irbesartan, representing a 34.9% difference between treatment arms (p=0.02).
  • C5b-9, a marker of complement pathway activation, decreased 50.2% with FILSPARI versus 7.3% with irbesartan, representing a 46.3% difference between treatment arms (p=0.032).
  • IL-6, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, decreased 45.4% with FILSPARI versus an 8.7% increase with irbesartan, representing a 49.7% difference between treatment arms (p<0.001).

The findings build on previously reported PROTECT results which demonstrated superior proteinuria reduction and a slower rate of kidney function decline with FILSPARI compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan. The consistency of effects across clinical outcomes and multiple biomarkers associated with IgAN disease biology provides further evidence that FILSPARI’s dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism may provide benefits beyond conventional RAS inhibition and supports its differentiated profile as an early, foundational, non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgAN.

More information on Travere’s presence at ASN Kidney Week can be found here.

About the PROTECT Study

The Phase 3 PROTECT Study was a global, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of FILSPARI compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan in 404 adults with biopsy-confirmed IgAN. Participants had urine protein excretion (UPE) ≥1.0 g/d and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² despite optimized renin-angiotensin system inhibitor therapy. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive FILSPARI 400 mg/day or irbesartan 300 mg/day for up to 110 weeks. The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in proteinuria from baseline at Week 36, and the key secondary efficacy endpoint was the rate of change in eGFR through Week 110.

About Travere Therapeutics

At Travere Therapeutics, we are in rare for life. We are a biopharmaceutical company that comes together every day to help patients, families and caregivers of all backgrounds as they navigate life with a rare disease. On this path, we know the need for treatment options is urgent – that is why our global team works with the rare disease community to identify, develop and deliver life-changing therapies. In pursuit of this mission, we continuously seek to understand the diverse perspectives of rare patients and to courageously forge new paths to make a difference in their lives and provide hope – today and tomorrow. For more information, visit travere.com.

FILSPARI® (sparsentan) U.S. Indication

FILSPARI® (sparsentan) is indicated:

  • To slow kidney function decline in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk for disease progression.
  • To reduce proteinuria in adult and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) without nephrotic syndrome.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

BOXED WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY AND EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Under the FILSPARI REMS, prescribers, patients and pharmacies must enroll in the program.

Hepatotoxicity

Some Endothelin Receptor Antagonists (ERAs) have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. In clinical studies, elevations in aminotransferases (ALT or AST) of at least 3-times the Upper Limit of Normal (ULN) have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge.

Measure transaminases and bilirubin before initiating treatment and then every 3 months during treatment. Interrupt treatment and closely monitor patients who develop aminotransferase elevations more than 3x ULN.

FILSPARI should generally be avoided in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) at baseline because monitoring for hepatotoxicity may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

FILSPARI is contraindicated for use during pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm if used by pregnant patients. Therefore, in patients who can become pregnant, exclude pregnancy prior to initiation of FILSPARI. Advise use of effective contraception before the initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible.

Contraindications

FILSPARI is contraindicated in patients who are pregnant. Do not coadminister FILSPARI with angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), ERAs, or aliskiren.

Warnings and Precautions

  • Hepatotoxicity: Elevations in ALT or AST of at least 3-fold ULN have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge. While no concurrent elevations in bilirubin >2-times ULN or cases of liver failure were observed in FILSPARI-treated patients in clinical trials, some ERAs have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. To reduce the risk of potential serious hepatotoxicity, measure serum aminotransferase levels and total bilirubin prior to initiation of treatment and then every 3 months during treatment.

    Advise patients with symptoms suggesting hepatotoxicity (nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, fatigue, anorexia, jaundice, dark urine, fever, or itching) to immediately stop treatment with FILSPARI and seek medical attention. If aminotransferase levels are abnormal at any time during treatment, interrupt FILSPARI and monitor as recommended.

    Consider re-initiation of FILSPARI only when hepatic enzyme levels and bilirubin return to pretreatment values and only in patients who have not experienced clinical symptoms of hepatotoxicity. Avoid initiation of FILSPARI in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) because monitoring hepatotoxicity in these patients may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity.
  • FILSPARI REMS: Due to the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Prescribers, patients, and pharmacies must be enrolled in the REMS program and comply with all requirements (www.filsparirems.com).
  • Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Based on data from animal reproduction studies, FILSPARI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant patient and is contraindicated during pregnancy. The available human data for ERAs do not establish the presence or absence of fetal harm related to the use of FILSPARI. Counsel patients who can become pregnant of the potential risk to a fetus. Exclude pregnancy before initiating treatment with FILSPARI. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. Advise pre-pubertal females and/or their guardian(s) of the fetal risk and the need to use effective contraception once they reach reproductive potential. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible.
  • Hypotension: Hypotension has been observed in patients treated with ARBs and ERAs and was observed in FILSPARI clinical studies. There was a greater incidence of hypotension-associated adverse events, some serious, including dizziness, in patients treated with FILSPARI compared to irbesartan. In patients at risk for hypotension, consider eliminating or adjusting other antihypertensive medications and maintaining appropriate volume status. If hypotension develops, despite elimination or reduction of other antihypertensive medications, consider a dose reduction or dose interruption of FILSPARI. A transient hypotensive response is not a contraindication to further dosing of FILSPARI, which can be given once blood pressure has stabilized.
  • Acute Kidney Injury: Monitor kidney function periodically. Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) can cause kidney injury. Patients whose kidney function may depend in part on the activity of the RAS (e.g., patients with renal artery stenosis, chronic kidney disease, severe congestive heart failure, or volume depletion) may be at particular risk of developing acute kidney injury on FILSPARI. Consider withholding or discontinuing therapy in patients who develop a clinically significant decrease in kidney function while on FILSPARI.
  • Hyperkalemia: Monitor serum potassium periodically and treat appropriately. Patients with advanced kidney disease, taking concomitant potassium-increasing drugs (e.g., potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics), or using potassium-containing salt substitutes are at increased risk for developing hyperkalemia. Dosage reduction or discontinuation of FILSPARI may be required.
  • Fluid Retention: Fluid retention may occur with ERAs and has been observed in clinical studies with FILSPARI. FILSPARI has not been evaluated in patients with heart failure. If clinically significant fluid retention develops, evaluate the patient to determine the cause and the potential need to initiate or modify the dose of diuretic treatment then consider modifying the dose of FILSPARI.

Adverse Reactions

  • IgAN patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are hyperkalemia, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), peripheral edema, dizziness, anemia, and acute kidney injury.
  • FSGS patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are peripheral edema, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), hyperkalemia, dizziness, and anemia.

Drug Interactions

  • Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS) Inhibitors and ERAs: Do not coadminister FILSPARI with ARBs, ERAs, or aliskiren due to increased risks of hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure).
  • Strong and Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors: Avoid concomitant use of FILSPARI with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, interrupt FILSPARI treatment. When resuming treatment with FILSPARI, consider dose titration. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly when used concomitantly with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inhibitor increases sparsentan exposure which may increase the risk of FILSPARI adverse reactions.
  • Strong CYP3A Inducers: Avoid concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inducer. Concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inducer decreases sparsentan exposure which may reduce FILSPARI efficacy.
  • Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents (NSAIDs), Including Selective Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) Inhibitors: Monitor for signs of worsening renal function with concomitant use with NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors). In patients with volume depletion (including those on diuretic therapy) or with impaired kidney function, concomitant use of NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors) with drugs that antagonize the angiotensin II receptor may result in deterioration of kidney function, including possible kidney failure. These effects are usually reversible.
  • CYP2B6, 2C9, and 2C19 Substrates: Monitor for efficacy of concurrently administered CYP2B6, 2C9, and 2C19 substrates and consider dosage adjustment in accordance with the Prescribing Information. Sparsentan is a weak inducer of CYP2B6 and 2C9, and a moderate inducer of 2C19. Sparsentan decreases exposure of these substrates, which may reduce efficacy related to these substrates.
  • P-gp Substrates: Monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates with narrow therapeutic indices when co-administered with FILSPARI. FILSPARI is a weak P-gp inhibitor and may increase plasma concentrations of P-gp substrate drugs.
  • Agents Increasing Serum Potassium: Monitor serum potassium frequently in patients treated with FILSPARI and other agents that increase serum potassium. Concomitant use of FILSPARI with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, or other drugs that raise serum potassium levels may result in hyperkalemia.

Key Terms

iga nephropathymedical
A kidney disease caused when deposits of the antibody called IgA collect in the tiny filters of the kidney, gradually reducing their ability to clear waste — like grit building up in a water filter. It matters to investors because it creates demand for diagnostics, drugs and long‑term care, drives clinical trial activity and regulatory decisions, and can influence the financial outlook of companies in pharma, biotech, medical devices and health insurance.
scd163medical
sCD163 is the soluble form of the cell-surface receptor CD163, a protein produced and shed by activated macrophages and monocytes; it is measured in blood as a biomarker of macrophage activation and certain inflammatory or immune processes. Levels rise when macrophages are activated or when CD163 is cleaved from cell surfaces, so sCD163 is used in clinical studies to indicate immune activation, inflammation, or disease activity, but its meaning depends on the clinical context and the specific laboratory assay used.
baffmedical
BAFF is a naturally occurring protein that helps certain immune cells (B cells) grow, survive and produce antibodies; think of it as a fertilizer that encourages those cells to multiply. It matters to investors because drugs that block or enhance BAFF can change the course of autoimmune diseases or B‑cell cancers, so clinical results, approvals or partnerships tied to BAFF-related therapies can strongly affect a biotech company’s value and prospects.
c5b-9medical
The C5b-9 complex is the terminal assembly of the complement cascade—formed when cleavage product C5 binds C6, C7, C8 and multiple C9 molecules—and is also called the membrane attack complex (MAC). When inserted into a cell or pathogen membrane it creates a pore that can disrupt membrane integrity; a soluble form (sC5b-9) circulates in blood and is measured as a biomarker of complement activation. Detection of C5b-9 indicates activation of the terminal complement pathway but does not by itself prove that target cells were killed, since complexes can be formed and cleared without cell lysis.
il-6medical
Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a small signaling protein the body releases as an alarm during infection, injury, or chronic inflammation; think of it as a smoke detector that calls immune cells to action. It matters to investors because IL-6 levels can serve as a biomarker for disease severity and a target for therapies—drugs that block or modulate IL-6 can change treatment outcomes, regulatory decisions, and commercial prospects in healthcare markets.

TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Caldwell (TSX:CWL)(OTCQX:CWLPF), a leading retained executive search firm, today announced it has completed the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of its wholly owned subsidiary, IQTalent Partners, Inc., to WinMil, Inc. WinMil will continue to operate the business under the IQTalent name and brand.

Caldwell acquired IQTalent in 2020 to broaden its service offerings into technology-enabled recruiting solutions at the professional level. After nearly six years, Caldwell determined that the business was not meeting the firm's strategic objectives and that a sale would better align its portfolio with its long-term priorities.

"Divesting IQTalent enables us to sharpen our focus on what Caldwell does best: delivering elite executive search and advisory services to our clients," said Chris Beck, chief executive officer of Caldwell. "IQTalent has been an important part of our portfolio, and we are proud of the innovative team and platform we helped build. We believe the business is well-positioned to succeed under WinMil's ownership, and we look forward to continuing a collaborative relationship through our referral partnership."

Founded in 2009, IQTalent pioneered an on-demand recruiting services model that blends proprietary technology with human expertise to deliver scalable talent acquisition solutions.

Transaction Terms

The transaction included the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of IQTalent. Under the terms of the agreement, total consideration at closing was approximately $4.7 million, consisting of:

  • $3.2 million in cash, subject to exchange rate changes and a net working capital adjustment; and
  • 1.45 million Caldwell common shares held by David Windley and Tom Milic, who are owners of WinMil and former employees of IQTalent. The shares were valued at approximately $1.5 million, based on a simple average price of $1.05 per Caldwell share over the 20 days prior to closing. The shares have been cancelled by Caldwell, reducing total shares outstanding by approximately 4.9%.

All dollar amounts are presented in Canadian dollars.

Caldwell retains its minority equity interest in the recruitment software company HootRecruit (formerly known as IQRecruit). Caldwell also retains the ability to utilize IQTalent's remaining deferred tax assets to apply against future taxable ordinary income generated by Caldwell in the United States.

Caldwell and WinMil have also entered into a two-year referral agreement to connect clients with the firms' complementary executive search and recruiting services.

Caldwell's Board of Directors will evaluate the use of the cash proceeds as part of its capital allocation planning and expects to provide an update with the release of Caldwell's next quarterly earnings.

GARDEN GROVE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--US Metro Bancorp (OTCQX: USMT): US Metro Bancorp (“Bancorp”) is a bank holding company, with a single subsidiary, US Metro Bank (“Bank”). On a consolidated basis, Bancorp earned $3.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $3.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. For the nine months ending September 30, 2026, the consolidated Bancorp earned $9.9 million compared to $8.0 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. On a year-to-date basis, Bancorp recorded an annualized return on average assets (“ROAA”) of 0.80% and an annualized return on average equity (“ROAE”) of 11.32%. With 16,791,500 shares outstanding, earnings per share (“EPS”) for the third quarter of 2026 was $0.19 compared to $0.21 in the second quarter of 2026. For the nine months ending September 30, 2026, EPS was $0.59 compared to $0.48 for the nine months ending September 30, 2025. On September 30, 2026, Bancorp’s book value per share was $7.06 compared to $6.62 a year earlier.

The Bank recorded on a year-to-date basis net interest income of $39.9 million compared to $33.1 million in the same period a year earlier. Net income of $11.7 million for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, compared to $9.2 million reported for the same nine months in 2025, a year over year increase of $2.55 million.

The Bank reported total assets of $1.730 billion as of September 30, 2026, representing a 10.2% increase compared to the reporting period ending September 30, 2025, and year over year loan growth of $157 million or 12.4%. Total Bank deposits ended the third quarter of 2026 at $1.527 billion, a $143 million or 10.3% increase from $1.384 billion on September 30, 2025.

Non-performing assets as a percentage of total assets of 1.39% on September 30, 2026, compared to 1.46% as of September 30, 2025. Allowance for credit losses (ACL) to gross loans was 1.25% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 1.19% as of September 30, 2025. The Bank recorded a $7.6 million provision for credit losses, for the nine months ending September 30, 2026, compared to $2.2 million recorded for the nine months ending September 30, 2025.

“Our third quarter results reflect the continued strength of our core franchise. Year-to-date earnings of $9.9 million are up 24% over the same period last year, and we delivered double-digit year-over-year growth in loans, deposits, and total assets. ALISO VIEJO, Calif., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- RxSight, Inc. (NASDAQ: RXST) today announced that on October 23, 2026, RxSight granted inducement stock options to purchase a total of 236,456 shares of RxSight’s common stock to two new non-executive officer employees in connection with the commencement of their employment with RxSight. RxSight also agreed to grant inducement restricted stock units (RSUs) covering a total of 637,449 shares of RxSight’s common stock to the same employees in connection with the commencement of their employment with RxSight, which RSUs are anticipated to be granted on or about November 3, 2026.

Each inducement stock option has an exercise price of $5.02 per share, which is equal to the closing price of a share of RxSight common stock on the grant date, and shall vest as follows, subject to continuing service: 25% of the shares subject to such inducement stock option shall vest on the one year anniversary of October 23, 2026, and one forty-eighth (1/48th) of the shares subject to such inducement stock option shall vest monthly thereafter.

Each inducement RSU award shall vest as follows, subject to continuing service: one-sixth of the shares subject to the inducement RSU award shall vest on the first trading day on or after each of February 28, 2027, August 31, 2027, February 29, 2028, August 31, 2028, February 28, 2029, and August 31, 2029.

Each inducement award is subject to the terms of the RxSight, Inc. 2026 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan and related forms of agreements, and were granted as inducements material to these employees to enter into employment with RxSight in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

About RxSight, Inc.

RxSight, Inc. is an ophthalmic medical device company dedicated to providing high-quality customized vision to patients following cataract surgery. The Light Adjustable Lens™ system, comprised of the RxSight Light Adjustable Lens™ products (LAL™ and LAL+™), RxSight Light Delivery Device™ (LDD™), and accessories, is the first and only commercially available intraocular lens (IOL) technology that can be adjusted after surgery, enabling doctors to customize and deliver high-quality vision to patients after cataract surgery. Additional information about RxSight can be found at www.rxsight.com.

Light Adjustable Lens™, LAL™, LAL+™, Light Delivery Device™ and LDD™ are trademarks of RxSight, Inc.
